answer: Each account privately receives a memory token every epoch, such as a word like orchard, dune or pearl paired with a hidden number, and later rounds randomly ask it to recall one from up to 20 epochs back. An honest agent stores a few bytes. An operator running 1,000 fakes must keep 1,000 separate histories, and one wrong recall forfeits that account's 10 POA bond, so a 5% error rate burns 500 POA per audit. Colluders cannot pool one memory: tokens are unique per account, so a shared answer exposes the link.
